The West African Examinations Council has opened registration for the 2027 West African Senior School Certificate Examination for School Candidates. The examination body announced the commencement of registration in a statement shared on its official account on Tuesday. “WASSCE for School Candidates, 2027: Registration is now open! WAEC is making examination preparation smarter and more accessible,” the council said. It urged schools to “complete their CASS uploads promptly and adhere strictly to all stipulated registration timelines.” The examination body also announced that the 2027 examination would be conducted in a hybrid mode. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources “Important: The 2027 examination will be conducted in hybrid mode,” it stated. WAEC began transitioning to computer-based examinations in 2024 with private candidates through a hybrid model in which multiple-choice questions were answered on-screen, while essay and practical papers remained manual. The examination body had earlier announced plans to fully implement computer-based examinations for school candidates in the May/June 2026 WASSCE, as part of efforts to modernise its assessment system, improve examination credibility and reduce malpractice. In October 2025, WAEC’s Head of National Office, Dr Amos Dangut, said the transition would help eliminate logistical challenges and improve the timeliness and credibility of examinations. He said, “Computer-based examinations will reduce fraud, examination malpractice. The records are there. For all five examinations we have conducted using CBT, there was a low rate of examination malpractice and higher performance of candidates. So, there is nothing to be afraid of.” The PUNCH had reported that the council also planned to provide schools with access to a testing portal to familiarise candidates with the system ahead of the examinations.
